# Installing and updating

Deaftly needs Android 8 or newer. You download it from the Deaftly website and install it yourself.

## Install

1. On your phone, open the [download page](https://deaftly.com/download/) and tap the download button. Your phone may warn that this type of file can harm your device. That warning appears for every app installed this way. Tap **Download anyway** if you're happy to continue.
2. When the download finishes, tap **Open**, or open the file from your Downloads folder.
3. Android will say it can't install apps from this source. Tap **Settings**, then switch on **Allow from this source** for the app you used to download the file, such as Chrome or Files. Go back and tap **Install**.
4. When it says the app is installed, tap **Open**.
5. You can now switch **Allow from this source** off again. Doing so doesn't affect Deaftly.

The wording and menu names differ between phone makers. If you can't see the option, open Settings and search for "Install unknown apps".

## Update

Deaftly doesn't update itself. When a new version is out:

1. Download the new file from the download page, as above.
2. Open it and tap **Update** or **Install**.

The new version installs over the old one. Your templates and settings are kept.

## Check it's genuine

Only install Deaftly from the download page. Copies from anywhere else may be fakes.

If Android says the app can't be installed because it conflicts with an existing package, or that the signatures don't match, stop. It means the file was signed with a different key from the app you already have, so it didn't come from Deaftly. Don't uninstall your copy to get around it. Download the file again from the download page.

Every official release is signed with the same key. If you're comfortable with developer tools, the download page shows its fingerprint so you can check it.
